question.problem: Find the directional derivative of the function $f(x,y)=(2{x}^{2}-y)^{2}$ at the point $A(-1,1)$ in the direction towards the point $B(-2,2).$
question.worked_solution:
The directional derivative ${f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)$ of a function $f(x,y)$ at the point $(a,b)$ in the direction of the vector $v$ is given by

$$
{f}_{u}^{′}(a,b)=∇f(a,b)\cdot u
$$

where $u$ is a unit vector in the direction of $v.$

First, we find the direction vector and the corresponding unit vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨-2,2⟩-⟨-1,1⟩ \\  & =⟨-1,1⟩ \\ u & =\frac{\overset{\to }{AB}}{‖\overset{\to }{AB}‖} \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{(-1)^{2}+{1}^{2}}}⟨-1,1⟩ \\  & =\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟨-1,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we calculate the gradient $∇f(x,y)$ and evaluate it at the point $A(-1,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}∇f(x,y) & =⟨\frac{∂}{∂x}(2{x}^{2}-y)^{2},\,\frac{∂}{∂y}(2{x}^{2}-y)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨16{x}^{3}-8xy,\,2y-4{x}^{2}⟩ \\ ∇f(-1,1) & =⟨16(-1)^{3}-8(-1)(1),\,2(1)-4(-1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨-8,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the directional derivative is

$$
\begin{aligned}{f}_{u}^{′}(-1,1) & =∇f(-1,1)\cdot u \\  & =⟨-8,-2⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}},\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}⟩ \\  & =(-8)\cdot (-\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}})-2\cdot (\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}) \\  & =\frac{6}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =3\sqrt{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
